ranked_facts.concept_key: Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles
ranked_facts.why: The presence of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles is more characteristic of Eosinophilic Fasciitis than Morphea (Localized Scleroderma), as the latter typically presents with more linear or band-like collagen deposition.

ranked_facts.concept_key: No appreciable skin tightening in affected areas
ranked_facts.why: The absence of appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas is more consistent with Eosinophilic Fasciitis, as Systemic Sclerosis-related Cutaneous Fibrosis typically presents with significant skin tightening due to the underlying fibrotic process.
